kurz: Cabbage with about 2 % salt ferments into sauerkraut in three to four weeks. Lactic acid bacteria make it sour and long-lasting.
bild_im_kopf: Like a castle training its own guards: the salt keeps strangers out until the lactic acid bacteria take over the gate.
sicherheit: Skim off a white film on the brine (kahm yeast). Furry, coloured mould or a rotten smell: throw it away.
material: 20 g non-iodised salt (about 2 % of the cabbage weight)
weight to press it down, clean cloth
verwendung: Raw as a salad: full of live bacteria.
Cooked with sausage, bacon and potatoes.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Slice the cabbage finely and knead it hard with the salt
schluesselmomente.warum: [[salz|Salt]] draws juice out of the cells. After a few minutes the cabbage is standing in its own brine.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Press it firmly into the jar until brine covers it, then weigh it down
schluesselmomente.warum: Under the brine there is no oxygen: mould cannot grow, but lactic acid bacteria can.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Leave at about 21–24 °C, always keeping the cabbage under the brine
schluesselmomente.warum: The bacteria make lactic acid. Warmer and it turns soft; below about 15 °C it hardly ferments.

schluesselmomente.schritt: After 3–4 weeks, when it no longer bubbles, chill it
schluesselmomente.warum: The acidity is now so high that hardly any germ can grow.
